blocks.title: <ico-recycle></ico-recycle> REPASO EXPRESS · lección anterior
blocks.intro: Antes de empezar, recupera lo de la clase pasada. Une cada verbo con su significado, sin mirar atrás.

blocks.title: <ico-book></ico-book> IF WE WERE TO… PROVIDED THAT…
blocks.intro: Negociar es poner condiciones. Aquí tienes tres herramientas: were to para tantear sin comprometerte, cuatro conectores de condición, y el tercer condicional para analizar el trato cuando ya terminó.

vocab.en: I can't go higher than that.
vocab.sp: no puedo subir más que eso

vocab.en: What would you have done differently?

blocks.note: Cómo funciona: tarjetas , diálogo, escucha , completar , comparar y ordenar . CHECK donde lo veas.

parts.html: 1 · LO QUE YA SABES DE B1 — oferta real y oferta hipotética

items.en: If you sign today, we'll give you 10% off.
items.sp: Primer condicional: una oferta real, sobre la mesa.

items.en: If we had more time, we would add the app.
items.sp: Segundo condicional: hipotético, no está pasando.

parts.html: 2 · WERE TO: TANTEAR EL TERRENO — propones sin comprometerte

items.en: If we were to extend the contract, would you be willing to pay upfront?
items.sp: Si extendiéramos el contrato, ¿estarían dispuestos a pagar por adelantado?

items.en: If we were to offer 10%, would you sign for two years?
items.sp: Todavía no ofreces nada: solo preguntas qué pasaría.

parts.body: If + were to + verbo, y en la otra mitad would. Es más suave que el primer condicional: si dicen que no, tú no ofreciste nada.

parts.html: 3 · CUATRO CONECTORES DE CONDICIÓN — siempre que, mientras, a menos que, si no

items.en: We can offer 10%, provided that you sign for two years.
items.sp: provided that = siempre que, con la condición de que.

items.en: The price stays the same as long as you're with us.
items.sp: as long as = mientras, siempre y cuando.

items.en: We can't lower the price unless you extend the contract.
We need an answer by Friday. Otherwise, the offer ends.
items.sp: otherwise = si no, de lo contrario. Empieza frase nueva y lleva coma.

parts.html: 4 · TERCER CONDICIONAL: EL ANÁLISIS — if + had + participio, would have + participio

items.en: If we hadn't offered the discount, he would have walked away.
items.sp: Si no hubiéramos ofrecido el descuento, se habría ido. (Pero lo ofrecimos.)

items.en: If we'd started with ten, we would have ended at fifteen.
I'd have asked for three years.
items.sp: Aquí I'd = I would. Suenan igual; la palabra siguiente te dice cuál es.

parts.html: 5 · LA FÓRMULA DEL INTERCAMBIO — doy esto, siempre que tú des aquello

items.en: We could deliver a month early, provided that the app moves to phase three.
items.sp: We could + lo que das, provided that you + lo que pides.

parts.html: TRAMPA DEL ESPAÑOL — tres calcos que se oyen en toda negociación

items.en: If I had known, I would have called.
items.sp: «Si hubiera sabido»: después de if va had, nunca would have.
Compromise = ceder un poco cada uno. «Compromiso» es commitment.

items.en: We need to discuss the price.

parts.body: If I would have known,… → If I had known,… · Let's discuss about the price. → Let's discuss the price.

blocks.title: <ico-star></ico-star> THE CONTRACT
blocks.intro: Día de la renovación. David quiere un 20% de descuento; el límite de Priya es 10%. Carla, que ya trabaja con el equipo, encontró el verdadero problema de David: su propia fecha límite.

cast.sp: lleva un dato a la mesa

blocks.title: DEAL WORDS · toca para girar
blocks.intro: Diez palabras que se oyen en cualquier mesa de negociación.

cards.back: una condición que rompe el trato
mejorar la oferta con un extra
en que ganan las dos partes

blocks.title: NAME YOUR PRICE
blocks.intro: Negocias tu tarifa como freelancer. Una respuesta cede demasiado, otra es demasiado dura y una es la correcta.

lines.html: Fifty dollars an hour? That's more than we planned to pay.

options: Oh, sorry. I can do it for twenty-five.
I understand. What budget did you have in mind?
Then find someone cheaper. Good luck.
I could do forty-five, provided that you book twenty hours a month.
Okay, thirty-five is fine, I guess.

lines.html: Twenty hours is a lot. What if we can only promise ten?

options: Then ten hours at thirty. No problem.
If you were to pay upfront, I'd be willing to do ten hours at forty-five.

lines.html: Upfront is fine. But we need the first project by Friday.

options: Friday works, as long as I get the materials tomorrow.
Friday? That's your problem, not mine.
Sure. I'll work all night if I have to.

lines.html: Deal. Can you put that in writing?

options: Oh, we don't need anything in writing. I trust you.
Of course. I'll send the terms today so you can sign off on them.

blocks.title: AUDIO 1 · THE TABLE
blocks.desc: David llega pidiendo 20%. Oferta, contraoferta, punto muerto… y un dato que cambia la conversación.

questions.q: What does David ask for first?
What is Priya's condition for the 10% discount?

options: Marcos offers to deliver phase two a month early

questions.q: Who conceded more on the discount?
options: David: he came down from 20% to 10%
Priya: she went up from 5% to 15%

speaking.prompt: Make the two trades yourself, as Priya and Marcos did: one with 'provided that', one with 'If we were to…'.
speaking.starter: We can offer (what), provided that you (condition). If we were to (idea), we could (benefit).

transcript.html: Let's not waste time. Twenty percent off, or I talk to the other agency.
Thank you for being direct, David. Twenty isn't possible. We could offer five.
Five? After the pricing incident? Fifteen is my bottom line.
And ten is ours. I can't go higher than ten.
Then we have a problem.
David, can I ask you something? Your board meets in September. And you promised them phase two before that meeting, didn't you?
Who told you that?
It was in your last email. So the real problem isn't the price. It's the date.
Go on.
If we were to move the mobile app to phase three, we could deliver phase two a month early. In August, before your board meets.
A month early. Hmm. And the discount?
We can offer ten percent, provided that you sign for two years instead of one.
Two years is a long time.
It is. But as long as you're with us, the price stays the same. No increases. Otherwise, we go back to a one-year contract at the normal rate.
Ten percent, two years, phase two in August, and the app waits.
That's the deal.
You know, I came here for twenty. Fine. Send me the terms. We have a deal.

blocks.title: SET THE CONDITION
blocks.intro: Elige el conector o la forma verbal que hace lógica la condición.

items.q: We can offer 10%, ___ you sign for two years.
We can't lower the price ___ you extend the contract.
We need an answer by Friday. ___, the offer ends.
The price stays the same ___ you're with us.
If we ___ deliver early, would you sign today?
If we ___ offered the discount, he would have walked away.
If she'd started with 10%, they ___ at 15%.
I won't sign ___ the terms are in writing.

blocks.title: IF WE EXTEND vs IF WE WERE TO EXTEND
blocks.intro: Las dos proponen lo mismo, pero una ya pone la oferta sobre la mesa y la otra solo explora la idea.

pair.a: If we extend the contract, will you pay upfront?
pair.b: If we were to extend the contract, would you be willing to pay upfront?

options: B — If we were to extend…
B — If we were to extend…

items.q: Con «were to», ¿qué va en la otra mitad de la frase?
Suaviza: «If you pay today, we'll give you 5% off.»
options: If you were to pay today, we would give you 5% off.
If you were pay today, we would give you 5% off.
If you would pay today, we will give you 5% off.
If we would sign for two years, would you lower the price?
If we were to sign for two years, would you lower the price?
If we were to sign for two years, will you lower the price?

blocks.title: LOOKING BACK AT THE DEAL
blocks.intro: Toca las palabras para armar frases con el tercer condicional: lo que habría pasado.

items.answer: If I had known, I would have called
He would have walked away if we had refused
If we had started with ten, we would have ended at fifteen
What would you have done differently?
I would have asked for three years

blocks.title: AUDIO 2 · THE DEBRIEF
blocks.desc: Después de la reunión, Carla y Marcos repasan el trato: qué salió bien y qué habrían hecho distinto.

questions.q: According to Carla, what would have happened if Priya had started at 10%?
Why does Carla think David was never going to walk away?
options: He needed the August date too much
He liked the team too much
The other agency was too expensive

questions.q: What would Carla have done differently?
What does Marcos's last line suggest?
options: He wants to negotiate alone next time
He wants Carla in the next negotiation
He thinks Carla talks too much

speaking.prompt: Think of a real negotiation of yours (a salary, a rent, a price). Say one thing you would have done differently.
speaking.starter: If I had (past participle), I would have (past participle). Next time, I'll (plan).

transcript.html: So? How did it go?
We have a deal. Ten percent, two years. And Carla, your tip about his board meeting saved us. If you hadn't found that email, we would have argued about the price all day.
I'm glad it helped. One thing, though. Priya opened at five percent, and you ended at ten. If she'd started with ten, you would have ended at fifteen.
True. And if David had walked away, we would have lost our biggest client.
He was never going to walk away. He needed that August date too much. That was your leverage.
What would you have done differently?
I'd have asked for three years. He would have said yes.
Next time, you're coming to the table with us.

blocks.title: <ico-pen></ico-pen> THE COUNTER-OFFER 2.0
blocks.intro: Un cliente (o tu jefe) te hizo una oferta que no te alcanza. Escribe tu contraoferta (5–7 frases): das algo, pides algo y dejas claro qué pasa si no hay acuerdo.
checklist: Agradece la oferta antes de responder (Thank you for…)
Un intercambio con We could…, provided that…
Una idea tanteada con If we were to…, would you be willing to…?
discuss sin about, y nada de if… would have
blocks.placeholder: Thank you for your offer of…
blocks.example: Thank you for su oferta. We could lo que das, provided that lo que pides. If we were to idea, would you be willing to verbo? Otherwise, la alternativa.
blocks.hw: Escribe tu contraoferta y después grábate diciéndola en voz alta, con calma y sin leer. Envíame texto y audio por WhatsApp.

rubric.d: Escribiste el número de frases que pide la consigna: agradeces, propones un intercambio y das la alternativa.
Usaste provided that, were to + would y otherwise / unless, bien formados.
Un lector lo entiende sin releer, y el tono es firme pero cordial.
